note: Original summaries written for SENTINEL-X. Technique identifiers reference the MITRE ATT&CK framework (attribution: MITRE ATT&CK, https://attack.mitre.org). No ATT&CK prose is copied; these are paraphrased, redistributable stubs for the first slice only.

documents.title: Brute Force (T1110)
documents.text: Brute force covers attempts to guess account credentials through many trials. A burst of failed authentications from a single source against one or many accounts, sometimes followed by a success, is a common signal. Sub-techniques include password guessing, password spraying and credential stuffing.

documents.title: Valid Accounts (T1078)
documents.text: Adversaries may use legitimate credentials to log in. A successful authentication immediately after many failures, or a login from an unusual source or time for the account, can indicate misuse of valid accounts rather than a benign login.

documents.title: Remote Services (T1021)
documents.text: Lateral movement via remote services (such as SSH or RDP) uses valid sessions to reach other hosts. Authentication to multiple internal hosts from one account in a short window can indicate lateral movement.

documents.title: Known benign: vulnerability scanners
documents.text: Scheduled internal vulnerability scanners can generate authentication failures and connection bursts that resemble attacks. Before escalating, check whether the source address belongs to an approved scanner inventory; if so the activity is typically a benign positive.
